stance_summary: Verified: New Zealand Q2 GDP printed 0.2% q/q and beat forecasts, parliament passed an India FTA covering about 95% of NZ exports, and NZDUSD sits at a 1y 12.9th / 5y 8.6th percentile after -3.90% 1m and -1.90% 5d while AUDUSD is only +0.20% 1m and AUDNZD is at a 5y 99.96th percentile. Inference: the market is still pricing an NZ labor/consumer recession (gauges 32/38) that the activity print and trade catalyst have already started to falsify, so the cleanest pro-cyclical expression is long the beaten-up NZD rather than paying already-hawkish US or CA STIR. Unknown: NZ policy path and CFTC/CME positioning are missing; temperature gauges are dashboard_v8 retained.

expression_comparison.rationale: Rates are the default when comparably clean; they are not comparably clean here. The discrepancy is NZ-specific (GDP beat plus India FTA versus NZDUSD at 1y 12.9th / 5y 8.6th percentile and AUDNZD at 5y 99.96th). NZ sovereign rates and NZ-US/AU-NZ RV are unavailable in this freeze, so the natural pay-NZ-rates expression cannot be marked. The substitute CA 2027 CORRA strip already prices about 111bp of additional tightening versus overnight 2.29 (and the full 3m CORRA curve peaks at 3.655, +136.5bp), while Canada August core inflation remaining near 2% is a live obstacle to paying more CA rates. The US substitute is worse: SOFR overnight 3.85, SR3U7 4.755 (+90.5bp), US 2Y 4.76 at a 1y 99.8th percentile after a delivered 25bp hike, so US growth strength is not the underpriced object. Spot NZDUSD is therefore the only markable instrument that owns the over-discounted NZ pessimism.

context_build.causal_mechanism: Test whether New Zealand activity and external demand are troughing while the FX market still prices a labor/consumer recession. Mechanism: a GDP beat plus a legally passed India FTA that cuts tariffs on about 95% of NZ exports should lift NZ growth, export receipts and risk appetite for NZD; with NZ rates unobservable, that repricing has to occur in NZDUSD. A secondary global support is the Saudi ship-to-ship crude workaround that reduced the extreme oil-supply tail, which should ease the risk-off bid in USD versus cyclicals rather than validate a growth break.

The damage is concentrated in the last month, not a three-month collapse. Cross-market path: AUDUSD +0.20% 1m at 1y 76th percentile, so this is not a generic USD bull against all cyclicals; AUDNZD +4.27% 1m / +2.05% 3m at 1y 99.80th and 5y 99.96th percentiles isolates NZD underperformance versus the regional cyclical. NZDCAD -2.22% 1m at 1y 20.4th percentile shows NZD lost to CAD as well. USDCHF +3.34% 1m and EURUSD -1.89% 1m show some USD strength, but AUD holding up means the NZD leg is the residual. context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known before this freeze: NZ labor 32 and consumer 38 were already weak, NZ inflation gauge 80 was already hot, and US activity/labor/inflation/consumer 69/75/72/74 already described a hot US. New in the 16 Sep cluster: NZ Q2 GDP 0.2% q/q beat forecasts; NZ parliament passed the India FTA; Saudi additional crude via Oman STS transfers; Fed delivered the widely priced 25bp hike; August US CPI had already kept the tightening bias intact. The known weak NZ labor/consumer gauges cannot by themselves explain a fresh 1m -3.90% NZDUSD dump that continues after the GDP beat and FTA; the new information is growth-positive for NZ and risk-positive for cyclicals, so the still-offered NZD is a lagged or over-discounted response.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: NZDUSD at 1y 12.9th / 5y 8.6th percentile with AUDNZD at a 5y extreme implies the market requires NZ to remain the weak cyclical: labor/consumer recession continues, the GDP beat is a one-off, and the India FTA does not lift receipts enough to matter versus a firm USD. On the USD leg, SR3 already requires further US tightening to a 4.755 Sep-27 implied peak and only about 24bp of subsequent easing by 2030, so the USD rate backdrop is high-for-long rather than a pending US easing cycle that would automatically rescue NZD.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: Disagree that NZ is in a self-reinforcing downturn that justifies 5y-cheap NZD versus both USD and AUD. The GDP beat and FTA are the start of a positive revision cycle; US growth remaining hot is a global demand support, not a reason to keep NZD at the 8.6th 5y percentile after a month of idiosyncratic underperformance.
context_build.price_decomposition: Level versus change: NZDUSD is cheap on 1y and 5y distributions (percentiles 12.9 / 8.6, z_1y -1.12, z_5y -1.15) but the 3m return is still +0.58%, so the stretch is a 1m/5d dump, not a completed multi-quarter collapse. Component: versus AUD (AUDNZD 1.2468, +4.27% 1m, 5y z 3.12) the move is NZD-specific; versus CAD (NZDCAD 0.8001, -2.22% 1m) it is also NZD-specific; versus a simple USD bid, AUDUSD's +0.20% 1m is the control. USD policy component: SOFR 3.85 and SR3U7 4.755 are the USD-rate leg; they explain some USD firmness but not why AUD held and NZD did not. Volatility: NZDUSD rv_20d 6.31 and rv_60d 7.21, so the 1m move is large relative to recent realized vol but not an untradeable blow-off. Percentiles are discovery flags only; the thesis is the GDP/FTA versus priced-recession gap.

policy_path_check.rationale: NZDUSD is a USD-funded cyclical. The US SOFR/SR3 path is required to know what the USD rate leg already prices (further hikes, not cuts). The CA CORRA path is required because the rates-first alternative is paying 2027 CORRA as a Canada growth-catch-up trade. NZ's own path is a known gap, which is exactly why the selected expression is spot NZDUSD rather than a NZ rates instrument.

trade.structure: Long NZDUSD spot versus USD at the frozen packet mid; unhedged to AUD or CAD so the NZ-specific residual versus AUDNZD/NZDCAD is retained.
trade.thesis: NZDUSD is pricing a New Zealand recession that the 16 Sep GDP beat and India FTA have already started to contradict, while US activity remains hot and the extreme oil-supply tail has been reduced. Growth, trade, and risk appetite are more resilient than a 5y-cheap NZD implies. The trade is long the cyclical that was sold, not mechanically long every high-beta currency: AUD is not cheap and Australia's housing channel is biting, and paying US or CA STIR fights curves that already embed large additional hikes.
trade.mispricing: Market prices NZ-specific stagnation (NZDUSD 5y 8.6th percentile, AUDNZD 5y 99.96th) as if labor 32 / consumer 38 dominate. That assumption is inconsistent with a GDP beat, an FTA covering about 95% of NZ exports, US gauges still 69-75, and a reduced oil-supply tail. The mispricing lives in NZDUSD because NZ rates cannot be marked.
